## Request
Build the canonical financial and KPI foundation for **TransDigm Group Incorporated**, as of **2024-09-30**, for the covenant_refinancing pathway. The requested comparison is FY2024 versus FY2023, in USD. This is an intermediate analytical handoff, not an investment recommendation or a legal opinion.

The financial base is consolidated historical reporting, not borrower-only financials. The annual filing reports the requested balance-sheet date retrospectively: the audit signature is dated November 7, 2024 (K, page:120). The information cutoff is Not supplied (C, page:1). Consequently this handoff does not certify what was publicly knowable on September 30, 2024. Subsequent settlements are identified separately. No external sources were used.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stronger earnings and operating cash flow coexist with higher gross leverage and substantial distribution commitments; historical financial analysis is usable, but legal headroom and refinancing execution are not established. | Medium | Governing agreements, forward cash assumptions and dated refinancing evidence are missing; the historical information cutoff is unspecified. |

| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gross debt / management adjusted earnings increased to 6.01x from 5.87x. | Earnings growth did not reduce gross balance-sheet leverage. | High |
| Cash flow after capital expenditures increased to US$1,880 million from US$1,236 million. | Better internal cash generation is offset by acquisition and shareholder-payment demands. | High |
| Year-end cash includes funds subsequently paid to shareholders and option holders. | Reported cash overstates the cash remaining after the disclosed settlements. | High |
| The reported maturity schedule uses fiscal years, not calendar years, and excludes finance leases and receivables borrowing. | Refinancing analysis needs the separate receivables renewal and an instrument-level schedule. | High |
| Management reports covenant compliance; independent contractual headroom is not calculable. | Accounting leverage cannot be used as legal covenant capacity. | High |

### Financial base view
The consolidated annual statements support a historical financial base and bounded refinancing preparation. Operating earnings and cash generation improved, but gross leverage increased and distributions consume cash that otherwise could reduce debt. Reported year-end cash is not post-dividend cash. Covenant capacity and forward refinancing access remain unverified.

Every displayed balance-sheet observation was reviewed for funding character. Assets, equity and long-term debt are not recast as non-debt funding stories. The material separately printed non-debt liability details are dividends payable and deferred income taxes, for both instants. For dividends payable, FY2024's US$4,216 million is a declared shareholder claim awaiting payment; FY2023 shows a dash. It is neither extra financial debt in the leverage numerator nor unencumbered surplus cash. K page:63 says it was settled on October 18, 2024. The same page identifies US$132 million of associated option-holder dividend equivalents accrued at year-end and subsequently paid; that amount is not assumed to equal the entire dividend-equivalent liability below.

For deferred income taxes, US$766 million in FY2024 and US$627 million in FY2023 represent a separately classified accounting liability rather than drawn financing (K page:120). They may affect future cash taxes, but no cash-release or settlement schedule is supplied in the inspected evidence. They are excluded from financial debt and no immediate liquidity benefit is inferred. The CFS deferred-tax adjustments are separately reported below and are not a repayment schedule for these balances.

Customer funding at US$168 million versus US$79 million provides timing support but entails delivery obligations; it is not permanent capital or an unconditional source for distributions. Other current and non-current liability classifications are retained; absent settlement details restrict liquidity stress analysis rather than the bounded reported balance-sheet summary.

Pricing conversions from source percentages to basis-point notation are unit representations, not financial aggregates. Notes retain their fixed percent coupons in the instrument names. That statement is not substituted for the annual maturity table or multiplied into an assumed forward amortization schedule.

**Precision exception.** The canonical gross debt calculation uses the USD-million gross debt-note observations, including receivables borrowing of 487. K page:62 says “the total drawn on the Securitization Facility is $487.5 million”, while K page:150 says “the total drawn on the Securitization Facility is $487 million.” The 486 balance-sheet value additionally reflects issuance costs. Preserve all three quantity/basis distinctions; exact drawn principal at sub-million precision remains conflicting for that purpose. Do not add the availability amount to historical cash.

**Entity boundary.** K page:124 states “TD Group has no significant assets or operations other than its 100% ownership of TransDigm Inc.” K page:151 identifies “TransDigm Inc., as issuer” for the 2033 notes. K page:153 gives classes of guarantors, with guarantor equivalence expressly “As of the date of this Form 10-K”. These do not establish an individually enumerated September guarantor roster. The partial issuer/guarantor summary encountered on K page:59 is not used as consolidated financial evidence or as a complete legal-perimeter financial package.

### Evidence-based credit interpretation
**Leverage.** Gross financial debt / EBITDA As Defined increased to 6.01x from 5.87x, whereas net leverage using reported year-end cash decreased to 4.51x from 4.84x. Both are calculated, not reported contractual metrics. For TransDigm Group Incorporated, the apparent net-leverage improvement is less durable than a debt repayment because cash was awaiting a declared distribution. Gross leverage also depends on management adjustments: using issuer EBITDA instead produces 6.57x versus 6.33x. This increases the importance of recurring cash earnings and control over further capital returns, rather than relying on headline net debt.

**Coverage.** Management adjusted EBITDA / net interest expense improved to 3.24x from 2.92x and the cash-interest proxy improved to 3.60x from 2.93x. However, the two interest numerators differ in accrual, netting and debt-cost amortization treatment. They do not demonstrate quarterly debt-service headroom, hedge effectiveness or forward financing costs. TransDigm's floating-rate term debt and separate receivables facility require their own prospective interest assumptions; no current SOFR path or forward hedge cash schedule is assumed.

**Cash-flow quality and capital allocation.** CFO rose from US$1,375 million to US$2,045 million and CFO less capex from US$1,236 million to US$1,880 million. The calculated cash-demand diagnostic after acquisitions and cash dividends/equivalents is negative US$2,505 million in FY2024 versus positive US$436 million in FY2023. This does not equate that diagnostic to the cash change: financing, option exercises, other investing items and FX also matter. It shows why stronger operating cash flow did not eliminate external funding needs. The cash-flow statement reports US$3,171 million of financing inflow in FY2024 (K page:123). K page:151 expressly links the September notes and Tranche L proceeds, together with cash on hand, to the special dividend declaration. The issuer-specific creditor risk is that substantial cash generation and incremental borrowing can fund distributions instead of reducing refinancing exposure.

**Earnings-definition quality.** The US$360 million FY2024 adjustment block versus US$247 million in FY2023 includes stock/deferred compensation and refinancing expenses present in both years. Acquisition-related adjustments contain multiple economic types, and the “Other, net” line is not sufficiently disaggregated to prove recurrence or cash realization. These observations support a challenge of the adjusted denominator, not an arbitrary haircut. No adjustment is declared invalid solely because it recurs; no legal EBITDA addback permission is inferred.

**Liquidity and separately dated events.** Year-end cash was US$6,261 million, and reported revolver availability was US$843 million. K page:63 discloses an October 16, 2024 receivables draw of US$162.5 million and October 18, 2024 payments of US$4,216 million to shareholders and US$132 million to eligible option holders. A deliberately bounded event-only cash illustration is US$2,075.5 million after those items, ignoring every other subsequent cash movement. That is not actual October closing cash or a cash-runway forecast. The equity distribution liability and subsequent payments make the reporting-date liquidity stock materially different from post-settlement operating flexibility. No assertion is made that every consolidated dollar can be transferred to the issuer or guarantors.

**Maturity/refinancing.** The source fiscal-year schedule places US$6,637 million in FY2028, while the receivables facility needs separate attention in FY2025. A remote-looking chart therefore does not remove near-term renewal exposure. Fiscal-year labels, excluded finance leases and the separate receivables borrowing must survive every downstream chart and model. The “Thereafter” amount must not be allocated across years without an instrument/amortization build.

**Covenants and contrary evidence.** K page:62 says the company was in compliance as of September 30, 2024. It reports a revolver usage trigger above 40% of commitments, currently US$364 million, and a maximum consolidated net leverage ratio of 7.50x, or 8.00x for the specified post-material-acquisition period. It also summarizes incremental tests of 7.25x consolidated net leverage and 5.00x secured net debt. Those are attributed filing summaries, not independently confirmed terms. Reported revolver availability and letters of credit are not a compliance certificate or sufficient evidence of defined usage. Contractual net debt, cash caps, EBITDA adjustments, acquisition treatment, test dates and amendment interactions are Not supplied. Consequently legal headroom is Not calculable; subtracting this handoff's accounting leverage from a filing-summary threshold would be misleading.

The annual-period binding is FY2024 2023-10-01 through 2024-09-30 and FY2023 2022-10-01 through 2023-09-30; debt/cash inputs are the corresponding September 30 instants. Ratio denominators are strictly positive. Rounded dashboard ratios derive from the unrounded kernel output, not from rounded intermediate monetary values. Source alias K identifies the exact source/hash above.
